test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 30 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
Calculation:

Let the current age of the father be F and the current age of the son be S.

3 years ago, the father's age was 30 years more than twice the son's age.

We can express this as: F - 3 = 2(S - 3) + 30 

⇒ F - 3 = 2(S - 3) + 30 

⇒ F - 3 = 2S - 6 + 30 

⇒ F - 3 = 2S + 24 

⇒ F = 2S + 27 ----- (1)

Let after **t years** the father will be twice the son's age in the future:

⇒ F + t = 2(S + t) 

Substitute F = 2S + 27 from Equation 1:

⇒ 2S + 27 + t = 2(S + t) 

⇒ 2S + 27 + t = 2S + 2t 

⇒ 27 + t = 2t 

⇒ 27 = t 

**∴ The father will be twice the son's age after 27 years.**
